question_papers.paper_title: Set 1 - Minerals and Energy Resources: Mineral Classification & Metallic Ores

questions.question_text: Leading Manganese producer state?
Highest quality iron ore with 70% iron content?
Radioactive mineral in Kerala Monazite sands?
Balaghat mines in MP produce which mineral?
Mineral occurring in veins and lodes?
Ferrous vs Non-Ferrous minerals.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Ferrous: Contain iron content, support metallurgical industries (Iron Ore, Manganese). Non-Ferrous: Lack iron, provide conductivity/corrosion resistance (Bauxite, Copper).

questions.question_text: What is Magnetite?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Finest iron ore with up to 70% iron content and superior natural magnetic properties valuable in electrical industries.

questions.question_text: Five primary geological occurrences of minerals.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Veins & Lodes (Igneous/Metamorphic). 2. Beds & Layers (Sedimentary). 3. Residual mass of weathered surface rocks. 4. Placer deposits in valley sands. 5. Ocean waters & beds.

questions.question_text: Detailed breakdown of Iron Ore belts in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Odisha-Jharkhand Belt: High grade Hematite in Badampahar (Mayurbhanj/Kendujhar) & Gua/Noamundi.
2. Durg-Bastar-Chandrapur Belt: Bailadila range in Chhattisgarh producing super high grade Hematite exported to Japan/South Korea via Visakhapatnam.
3. Ballari-Chitradurga-Chikkamagaluru-Tumakuru Belt: Kudremukh deposits in Western Ghats transported as slurry via pipeline to Mangaluru port.
4. Maharashtra-Goa Belt: Ratnagiri and Goa mines exported via Marmagao port.

questions.case_passage:
Mining is called a 'Killer Industry' due to dust inhalation causing silicosis, mine collapses, and stream pollution.
Q1. Why termed 'Killer Industry'? (1m)
Q2. Health risks for miners? (2m)
Q3. Environmental impact of mine waste? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Poses acute health hazards, structural collapse risks, and environmental destruction.
2. Inhalation of toxic mineral dust causes pulmonary diseases like silicosis.
3. Dumping mine waste pollutes topsoil and renders streams acidic.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 2 - Minerals and Energy Resources: Energy Resources: Conventional vs Non-Conventional

questions.question_text: Oldest operating oilfield in India?
HVJ pipeline transports?
Solar energy potential is highest in?
Geothermal plant in Himachal Pradesh?
Gondwana coal age is approx?
Conventional vs Non-Conventional energy sources.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Conventional: Non-renewable fossil fuels (Coal, Petroleum, Natural Gas). Non-Conventional: Renewable clean energy (Solar, Wind, Tidal, Geothermal, Atomic).

questions.question_text: What is HVJ Pipeline?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Hazira-Vijaipur-Jagdishpur 1,700 km cross-country gas pipeline connecting gas fields in Mumbai High/Gujarat to inland fertilizer & power plants.

questions.question_text: Four commercial coal varieties in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Anthracite: Highest quality, hard coal (>80% carbon). 2. Bituminous: Most popular commercial metallurgical coal. 3. Lignite: Low grade brown coal, high moisture (Neyveli, TN). 4. Peat: Low carbon, high moisture, low heating capacity.

questions.question_text: Non-Conventional energy options in India: Solar, Wind, Biogas, Tidal, Geothermal.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Solar: Photovoltaic technology in Rajasthan/Gujarat.
Wind: Wind farm cluster from Nagarcoil to Madurai in Tamil Nadu.
Biogas: Gobar gas plants converting organic farm waste into clean fuel & manure.
Tidal: Oceanic tides harnessed in Gulf of Khambhat.
Geothermal: Subterranean steam driving turbines in Manikaran (HP) & Puga Valley (Ladakh).

questions.case_scenario_title: Case Study on Kudremukh Slurry Pipeline
questions.case_passage:
Kudremukh iron ore in Western Ghats was mined as slurry and transported through a pipeline to Mangaluru port.
Q1. Mine location? (1m)
Q2. How iron ore was transported? (2m)
Q3. Why mining stopped? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Kudremukh, Western Ghats, Karnataka.
2. Transported as liquid slurry through an underground pipeline to Mangaluru port.
3. Environmental concerns over biodiversity destruction in Western Ghats rainforest catchments.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 3 - Minerals and Energy Resources: Non-Metallic Minerals & Energy Conservation

questions.question_text: Mineral with excellent di-electric strength and low power loss?
Bauxite is the ore for which light metal?
Leading Mica producing belt?
Neyveli in Tamil Nadu is famous for?
Nuclear fuel element from Monazite sand?
Why Mica is indispensable in electrical and electronics industry.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Possesses high di-electric strength, low power loss factor, excellent insulating properties, and resistance to high voltage.

questions.question_text: How is Bauxite formed?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Forms by intense surface weathering and decomposition of rocks rich in aluminum silicates in tropical climates.

questions.question_text: Conservation of mineral resources imperative.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Minerals are non-renewable and require millions of years to form. Continued extraction depletes reserves and raises costs as deeper mining yields lower-grade ores. Recycling metals is essential.

questions.question_text: Analysis of Coal occurrence in India: Gondwana vs Tertiary.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Gondwana Coal: Formed over 200 million years ago. Metallurgical coking coal used in steel smelting. Located in Damodar valley (Jharia, Raniganj, Bokaro), Godavari, Mahanadi, Son valleys.
Tertiary Coal: Formed 55 million years ago. Found in North-Eastern states (Assam, Meghalaya, Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland).

questions.case_passage:
Solar energy utilizes photovoltaic technology converting sunlight directly into electricity, expanding in rural India.
Q1. Technology used? (1m)
Q2. Two advantages over thermal power? (2m)
Q3. Top state for solar plants? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Photovoltaic (PV) technology.
2. Non-polluting/zero carbon emissions and renewable.
3. Rajasthan.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 4 - Minerals and Energy Resources: Petroleum, Natural Gas & Wind Energy

questions.question_text: Major offshore oilfield of India?
Wind farm cluster state?
Clean energy fuel considered environment-friendly?
Geothermal plant in Ladakh?
Bailadila iron ore exported via port?
Why Natural Gas is considered the fuel of the 21st century.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Environment-friendly with low carbon dioxide emissions, flexible for power, fertilizer plants, and CNG for vehicles.

questions.question_text: What are Placer Deposits?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Alluvial mineral deposits in valley floor sands containing heavy non-corrosive metals (Gold, Silver, Platinum, Tin).

questions.question_text: Petroleum occurrences in geological structures.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Petroleum is trapped in anticlines and fault traps in tertiary rock formations. Oil-bearing layers are porous limestone or sandstone capped by non-porous rock.

questions.question_text: Strategy for sustainable energy use in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Promote public transport over individual vehicles. 2. Switch to renewable solar/wind energy. 3. Power saving via LED and efficient electrical devices. 4. Turn off electricity when not in use. 5. Recycle metals to save energy in smelting.

questions.case_scenario_title: Case Study on Biogas in Rural India
questions.case_passage:
Gobar gas plants convert cattle dung and organic waste into biogas, providing lighting and high-quality manure.
Q1. Feedstock for Gobar gas plants? (1m)
Q2. Twin benefits for farmers? (2m)
Q3. Environmental impact? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Cattle dung, farm waste, and domestic organic waste.
2. Clean cooking fuel/energy and nutrient-rich organic manure.
3. Prevents tree cutting for fuelwood and eliminates smoke pollution.

question_papers.paper_title: Set 5 - Minerals and Energy Resources: Comprehensive Mineral & Energy Infrastructure

questions.question_text: Atomic power station in Maharashtra?
Panchpatmali deposits in Koraput produce?
Copper mines in Rajasthan?
Metals made by recycling scrap are called?
Salt, magnesium, and bromine are extracted from?
Secondary metals definition.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Metals produced by recycling scrap metal products, saving energy and mineral reserves.

questions.question_text: Two atomic power stations in India.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Tarapur (Maharashtra) and Narora (Uttar Pradesh).

questions.question_text: Compare Magnetite and Hematite iron ores.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Magnetite: 70% iron content, high magnetic quality, black color, electrical industry use.
Hematite: 50-60% iron content, most important industrial iron ore, reddish brown color.

questions.question_text: Distribution of Non-Ferrous minerals: Bauxite and Copper.
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
Bauxite: Formed by surface rock leaching. Panchpatmali (Odisha), Amarkantak plateau (MP), Bilaspur-Katni. Used in aircraft, auto, utensils.
Copper: Malleable, ductile, conductor. Balaghat (MP), Khetri (Rajasthan), Singhbhum (Jharkhand). Used in electrical cables & electronics.

questions.case_passage:
'Energy saved is energy produced.' Sustainable development mandates energy conservation in domestic, industrial, and transport sectors.
Q1. Core message of slogan? (1m)
Q2. Three domestic conservation steps? (2m)
Q3. Transport sector measure? (1m)
questions.marking_scheme_answer:
1. Conserving existing energy reduces the need to generate non-renewable energy.
2. Using LED bulbs, switching off appliances when unused, choosing star-rated equipment.
3. Using public transport or carpooling instead of personal vehicles.
